extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examining patentability under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 (including special treatment under pre-AIA 103(b) for biotechnological processes) and transitional guidance for AIA 102/103. Covers when to make specific rejections, form paragraph usage, obviousness test factors, and election/timeliness rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(b) is applicable to biotechnological processes only; only applications subject to pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 are subject to pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2159 to determine whether an application is subject to pre-AIA examination. Pre-AIA 103(b) precludes rejection of process claims that involve the use or making of certain nonobvious biotechnological compositions of matter under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory requirements for pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(b) treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain pre-AIA 103(b) treatment a biotechnological process using or resulting in a composition that is novel under section 102 and nonobvious under 103(a) shall be considered nonobvious if: (1) claims to the process and the composition are contained in the same application or in separate applications having the same effective filing date; and (2) the composition and the process at the time invented were owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally: a patent issued on a process must also contain claims to the composition used in or made by that process, or if such composition is claimed in another patent, the process patent shall expire on the same date as the other patent. The biotechnological process must fall within the statutory definition and a timely election to proceed under pre-AIA 103(b) must be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'biotechnological process' under pre-AIA 103(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of pre-AIA 103(b), 'biotechnological process' means: (A) a process of genetically altering or otherwise inducing a single- or multi-celled organism to (i) express an exogenous nucleotide sequence, (ii) inhibit, eliminate, augment, or alter expression of an endogenous nucleotide sequence, or (iii) express a specific physiological characteristic not naturally associated with said organism; (B) cell fusion procedures yielding a cell line that expresses a specific protein (e.g., a monoclonal antibody); and (C) a method of using a product produced by such a process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statutory definition limits which processes qualify for 103(b) treatment; see the text for the enumerated subparts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election procedure and timeliness for pre-AIA 103(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: An election to proceed under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(b) must be made by way of petition under 37 CFR 1.182. The petition must establish that all statutory requirements have been satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An election will normally be considered timely if made no later than the earlier of either the payment of the issue fee or the filing of an appeal brief in an application which contains a composition of matter claim which has not been rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103(a). Special timeliness rules apply to certain applications pending around March 1996; see MPEP for those exceptions. If a patent is granted without an election due to error, a reissue may be filed to permit consideration of qualifying process claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on process patent term and composition claims under 103(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent issued on a process under pre-AIA 103(b)(1) shall also contain the claims to the composition of matter used in or made by that process, or shall, if such composition is claimed in another patent, be set to expire on the same date as such other patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory requirement ensures the process patent's term aligns with the composition patent when composition claims are in a different patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph ¶7.06 (Notice re prior art available under both pre-AIA and AIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a prior art rejection is made in an application with an actual filing date on or after March 16, 2013 that claims priority to, or the benefit of, an application filed before March 16, 2013, include ¶7.06 in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph should be used in all such Office Actions, but only once per Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ¶7.20.fti (Statement of Statutory Basis, pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a quotation of pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) when this statute forms the basis for an obviousness rejection in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute quotation is required in first actions on the merits employing pre-AIA 103(a) and in final rejections. It should be used only once in a given Office action and must precede form paragraphs 7.20.01.fti - 7.22.fti when used to cite the statute in first actions and final rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection using prior art disqualified under 103(c) but qualifying under another 102 subsection (¶7.20.01.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant has provided a submission claiming common ownership or joint research agreement yet the reference qualifies as prior art under another subsection of pre-AIA 102, the examiner should state that the reference is not disqualified and identify the common assignee and the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may overcome the applied art by a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that the invention in the reference was derived from the inventor, or by antedating under 37 CFR 1.131(a). When using this paragraph, identify the common assignee in bracket 1 and the disqualified reference in bracket 2. This paragraph must follow form paragraph 7.20.fti where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of common ownership for joint inventors (¶7.20.02.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application names joint inventors, the examiner presumes the subject matter of various claims was commonly owned at the time inventions were made absent evidence to the contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is advised of the duty under 37 CFR 1.56 to identify inventor and invention dates for any claim not commonly owned so the examiner can consider applicability of pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) and potential 102(e), (f) or (g) prior art. This paragraph must be used in all applications with joint inventors unless claims are clearly restricted to a single claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualification attempt deficiencies under 103(c) — common ownership (¶7.20.04.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant attempts to disqualify a reference under 103(c) by showing common ownership but fails to provide the required conspicuous statement, the reference is not disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must file the required submission to properly disqualify the reference under 103(c). Examiner should include this paragraph and may note that the applicant may also overcome the art under 37 CFR 1.132 or by antedating under 37 CFR 1.131(a). Identify the commonly owned applied art in the designated brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualification attempt deficiencies under 103(c) — joint research agreement (¶7.20.05.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant attempts to disqualify a reference under 103(c) by showing a joint research agreement but fails to meet statutory or rule requirements, the disqualification attempt is ineffective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must file the missing requirements (see 37 CFR 1.71(g) and 1.104(c)) and may overcome the applied art under 37 CFR 1.132 or by antedating under 37 CFR 1.131(a). Identify the reference and reason the attempt is ineffective in the designated brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph ¶7.21.fti — Rejection under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ¶7.21.fti to state that specific claims are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being unpatentable over identified prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.20.fti or 7.103. An explanation of the rejection must follow (see MPEP § 2144). If the rejection relies on prior art under pre-AIA 102(e), apply the amended pre-AIA 102(e) rules per AIPA to determine the reference's prior art date (with listed exceptions). Insert claim numbers and prior art in the designated brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional obviousness rejection based on copending application (¶7.21.01.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ¶7.21.01.fti to provisionally reject claims as obvious over a copending application that would be prior art under pre-AIA 102(e) if published or patented and that has a common assignee, common applicant, or at least one common (joint) inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provisional rejection is based on a presumption of future publication or patenting of the copending application. It may be overcome by: (1) a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that the invention disclosed was derived from the inventive entity of this application; (2) a showing of an earlier date of invention under 37 CFR 1.131(a); or (3) showing the copending application is disqualified under pre-AIA 103(c). Use appropriate procedures to determine the copending application’s 102(e) date (AIPA rules) as noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection using reference that has common assignee/applicant/joint inventor (¶7.21.02.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reference qualifies as prior art under pre-AIA 102(e) and has a common assignee, common applicant, or at least one common inventor, the claim(s) may be rejected under pre-AIA 103(a) over that reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection may be overcome by: (1) showing under 37 CFR 1.132 derivation of the reference from the applicant; (2) showing an earlier invention date under 37 CFR 1.131(a); or (3) an oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(c) and a terminal disclaimer per 37 CFR 1.321(c) where applicable. Use pre-AIPA 102(e) rules to determine the reference's date when appropriate. Insert claim numbers, reference, and identification (assignee/applicant/inventor) as directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test for Obviousness (Graham factors) (¶7.23.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: The factual inquiries for determining obviousness under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) are: (1) determining the scope and contents of the prior art; (2) ascertaining the differences between the prior art and the claims at issue; (3) resolving the level of ordinary skill in the pertinent art; (4) considering objective evidence (secondary considerations) indicating obviousness or nonobviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This summary of the Graham factors may be used, if appropriate, in response to arguments regarding the applicability of factors for determining obviousness. An explanation must follow when using form paragraphs that cite obviousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ¶7.27.fti — Combined rejection under pre-AIA 102 or pre-AIA 103(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶7.27.fti states a claim is rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 (specific paragraph) as anticipated or, in the alternative, under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as obvious over identified art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph is NOT intended to be commonly used as a substitute for proper separate rejections. Use separate rejections under 102 or 103 when possible. Examples where ¶7.27.fti may be appropriate include: disputed claim interpretation that could lead to either a 102 or 103 rejection; references that disclose all claim limitations except a property/function where inherency is uncertain; small genus/species issues; product-by-process variations; means-plus-function uncertainties; overlapping ranges without a specific example in the reference. A full explanation must follow and other form paragraphs must precede ¶7.27.fti as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued applicability of pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 and transitional rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The AIA revisions to 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 do not apply to any application filed before March 16, 2013; such applications remain governed by pre-AIA 102 and 103. Applications filed on or after March 16, 2013 may still be subject to pre-AIA 102 in certain situations (e.g., if they have never contained a claim with an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an RCE or entering national stage does not change an application's pre-AIA status. MPEP §§ 2131-2138 provide guidance on prior art available for pre-AIA applications. Use the application’s actual/ effective filing date and claim history to determine which regime applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA changes to prior art scope (AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) and (a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the AIA, AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) bars patents when the claimed invention was patented, described in a printed publication, or in public use, on sale, or otherwise available to the public before the effective filing date. AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) bars patents when the claimed invention was described in a patent or application published/issued naming another inventor and effectively filed before the claimed invention's effective filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AIA 102(a) revises what qualifies as prior art; see MPEP for applying these provisions in examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1) — one-year grace period and measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1) provides that disclosures made one year or less before the effective filing date shall not be prior art if: (1) the disclosure was made by the inventor/joint inventor or by another who obtained the subject matter directly/indirectly from the inventor; or (2) the subject matter had been publicly disclosed earlier by the inventor or someone who obtained it from the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The one-year grace period is measured from the filing date of the earliest U.S. or foreign patent application to which a proper benefit/priority claim has been asserted and that supports the claimed invention per 35 U.S.C. 112(a). The grace period is extended to the next business day if it would otherwise end on a weekend or federal holiday. Under the AIA the date of invention is not relevant for antedating prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA definitions relevant to 102/103 (claimed invention, effective filing date, inventor)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA 35 U.S.C. 100 defines 'claimed invention' as the subject matter defined by a claim; 'effective filing date' as the earlier of the actual filing date or the filing date of the earliest application to which benefit/priority is properly claimed (provided that earlier application supports the claimed invention per 35 U.S.C. 112(a)); 'inventor' and 'joint inventor' are defined as the individual(s) who invented or discovered the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions affect how prior art and grace-period rules are applied under the AIA; ensure claimed subject matter is supported in the earlier application per 112(a) when claiming benefit/priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and date-of-invention changes under the AIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Under pre-AIA 102(a)/(b) certain prior art activities had to occur in the United States to qualify; under the AIA there is no geographic requirement for prior public use, sale, or disclosure to be prior art. The date of invention is not relevant under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus antedating by showing an earlier date of invention (e.g., under 37 CFR 1.131) is not effective against AIA prior art; apply AIA provisions for determining prior art and exceptions instead.
